name: Crossroads Pipeline Expansion Project

values.RouteNotes: Scope is loops and extensions on the existing line plus added compression. No route has been published.
values.DataCenterNotes: No single data center campus is named for this expansion. The open season notice from Crossroads Pipeline Company, posted in February 2026, says the project responds to recently announced power generation and data center developments in the Midwest. It aims to serve markets in northern Indiana, Illinois, Iowa and South Dakota, with up to 1,500,000 dekatherms a day of capacity. Foundation shippers must commit at least 500,000 dekatherms a day for 20 years. Anchor shippers must commit at least 135,000 dekatherms a day for 20 years. The notice names no data center customer or shipper. The Energy Information Administration lists the demand served as power and data centers. A search found a $20 billion Joliet Technology Center in Illinois, but no source ties it to this project.

researcher_notes: This is an expansion of the existing Crossroads Gas Pipeline (P0172) that has no row of its own, so it is staged in the parent system and project shape. Crossroads Pipeline Co., owned by TC Energy, held a non-binding open season that started on February 9, 2026 for up to 1.5 billion cubic feet a day of added capacity. TC Energy said the open season was about 2.5 times oversubscribed. The target in-service date is November 2030, which depends on binding commitments. The Energy Information Administration August 2026 pipeline projects workbook (Natural Gas Pipeline Projects sheet, Excel row 32, project name Crossroads Expansion Project) lists it as Announced with 1,500 million cubic feet a day added and says the scope serves data-center and power demand. It lists Demand Served as Power/Data Centers. That is the basis for DataCenter = yes. An East Daley analyst note from February 2026 describes the same open season and the Illinois data center load, but it does not name a specific data center customer. The Energy Information Administration lists 200 miles, but that is the length of the existing line, not new pipe. The new pipe is unknown because the scope of loops and extensions is not set, so length is left blank. No cost, diameter or Federal Energy Regulatory Commission docket was found. Start and end are the Ohio and Indiana ends of the existing line, which is where the loops would be added. The new receipt point at Rover in Defiance, Ohio and delivery points near Joliet, Illinois and on Northern Border Pipeline are also in the East Daley note. The TC Energy first quarter 2026 release confirms the open season and its oversubscription, but its page would not load in the checker, so it is not cited. The concrete step is the open season only, so confidence is medium. The route is not published. Owner spelling was checked, with no close existing entity and no style change.
